questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Definite Integral Using the Constant Multiple Rule
questions.worked_solution:
Factoring the constant out of the integral, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{3}\frac{t}{8}\,\text{d}t & =\frac{1}{8}{\int }_{2}^{3}t\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{8}\cdot \frac{1}{2}{t}^{2}\,{|}_{2}^{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{16}\cdot {t}^{2}\,{|}_{2}^{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{16}({3}^{2}-{2}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{16}(9-4) \\  & =\frac{5}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,\text{d}\theta  & =-3{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =-3(-\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =3(\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =3[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡0] \\  & =3(0-1) \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}

questions.worked_solution:
Factoring the constant out of the integral, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{\sqrt{3}}\frac{5}{1+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =5{\int }_{1}^{\sqrt{3}}\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =5\cdot \text{arctan}\,x\,{|}_{1}^{\sqrt{3}} \\  & =5(\text{arctan}(\sqrt{3})-\text{arctan}(1)) \\  & =5(\frac{\pi }{3}-\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =5(\frac{\pi }{12}) \\  & =\frac{5\pi }{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating the Integral of the Sum of Two Functions Using the Sum Rule
questions.worked_solution:
Splitting up the integral into the difference of two integrals and evaluating each integral separately, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}(y-\frac{1}{{y}^{2}})\text{d}y & ={\int }_{1}^{2}y\,\text{d}y-{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}\,{|}_{1}^{2}+\frac{1}{y}\,{|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}({2}^{2}-{1}^{2})+(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{1}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(3)+(\frac{1}{2}-1) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}-\frac{1}{2} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating the Integral of the Sum of Two Functions Using the Sum Rule
questions.worked_solution:
Splitting up the integral into the difference of two integrals and evaluating each integral separately, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}({e}^{x}-\frac{1}{x})\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{e}{e}^{x}\,\text{d}x-{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={e}^{x}\,{|}_{1}^{e}-\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|\,{|}_{1}^{e} \\  & =({e}^{e}-{e}^{1})-(\operatorname{ln}⁡(e)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)) \\  & =({e}^{e}-e)-(1-0) \\  & ={e}^{e}-e-1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Splitting up the integral into the sum of two integrals and evaluating each integral separately, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}(2\cdot {3}^{x}+x)\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2\cdot {3}^{x}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{1}x\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\cdot \frac{{3}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\,{|}_{0}^{1}+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}\,{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}({3}^{1}-{3}^{0})+\frac{1}{2}({1}^{2}-{0}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}(3-1)+\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{4}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}({x}^{2}-\frac{1}{x})\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x-{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}\,{|}_{1}^{{e}^{2}}-\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|\,{|}_{1}^{{e}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(({e}^{2})^{3}-{1}^{3})-(\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{2})-\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}({e}^{6}-1)-(2-0) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{6}-1}{3}-2 \\  & =\frac{{e}^{6}-7}{3}.\end{aligned}

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating the Integral of a Polynomial Function
questions.worked_solution:
Splitting up the sum and factoring out the constants, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{2}(3z+2)\,\text{d}z & =3{\int }_{-2}^{2}z\,\text{d}z+2{\int }_{-2}^{2}\,\text{d}z \\  & =3\cdot \frac{{z}^{2}}{2}{|}_{-2}^{2}+2z\,{|}_{-2}^{2} \\  & =3(\frac{{2}^{2}}{2}-\frac{(-2)^{2}}{2})+2(2-(-2)) \\  & =3\cdot 0+2\cdot 4 \\  & =8.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating the Integral of a Sum of Two Functions
questions.worked_solution:
We split the integral into the sum of two integrals and factor out the constants. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }(2\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & =2{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =2(-\operatorname{cos}⁡x){|}_{0}^{\pi }+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,{|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =2[(-\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi )-(-\operatorname{cos}⁡0)]+(\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi -\operatorname{sin}⁡0) \\  & =2(1-(-1))+(0-0) \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Evaluate $\displaystyle \int_{0}^{\pi/4} (\sec x \tan x - \cos x)\, \textrm d x.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Splitting up the integral into the difference of two integrals and evaluating each integral separately, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}(\operatorname{sec}⁡x\operatorname{tan}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\operatorname{sec}⁡x\operatorname{tan}⁡x\,\text{d}x-{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{sec}⁡x\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /4}-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /4} \\  & =(\operatorname{sec}⁡\frac{\pi }{4}-\operatorname{sec}⁡0)-(\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi }{4}-\operatorname{sin}⁡0) \\  & =(\sqrt{2}-1)-(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}-0) \\  & =\sqrt{2}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}-1 \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{2}}{2}-1 \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}-1.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Evaluating the Integral of a Polynomial Function
Evaluating the Integral of a Sum of Two Functions
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the integral as

$$
\int_1^4 \left( \sqrt x - \dfrac 2 {x^2} \right) \, \textrm dx = \int_1^4 \left( x^{1/2}-2x^{-2} \right) \, \textrm dx.
$$

 

Then, we split the integral into the difference of two integrals and factor out the constants. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{4}(\sqrt{x}-\frac{2}{{x}^{2}})\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{4}{x}^{1/2}\,\text{d}x-2{\int }_{1}^{4}{x}^{-2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{3}{x}^{3/2}\,{|}_{1}^{4}+2{x}^{-1}\,{|}_{1}^{4} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}({4}^{3/2}-{1}^{3/2})+2({4}^{-1}-{1}^{-1}) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}(8-1)+2(\frac{1}{4}-1) \\  & =\frac{14}{3}+2\cdot (-\frac{3}{4}) \\  & =\frac{14}{3}-\frac{3}{2} \\  & =\frac{19}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$
